section_summary: This section records inquiries from American and Belgian holders of Japanese bonds and the State Department’s replies about defaults, claims, and possible treatment in a peace treaty. A substantial group of documents concerns electric utility bonds: wartime transfers of power assets, conversion of dollar bonds into yen bonds, cancellation of mortgages, and requests to restore bondholders’ security. It includes correspondence from banks and trustees, a Japanese company report, and a translation of Japan’s 1943 foreign bonds law.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Frank E. Rice
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains the Department’s position on Rice’s Imperial Japanese Government bond.
subfiles.summary: The Department directs Rice to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, notes uncertainty about a peace treaty, and requests purchase and citizenship details for its records.

subfiles.title: Frank E. Rice’s inquiry about an Imperial Japanese Government bond
subfiles.about: Asks what is being done for American owners of Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Rice identifies his $1,000 External Loan of 1924 bond and seeks guidance.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Alfred Hansen
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds concerning Imperial Japanese Government and Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes its limited assistance to bondholders, recommends the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, requests details for its records, and points to possible debt claims through the Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Alfred Hansen’s bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese government and Tokyo Electric Light bonds with unpaid coupons.
subfiles.summary: Hansen asks for advice on his two defaulted Japanese bond holdings.

subfiles.title: Dillon, Read & Co. request to restore electric utility mortgages
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests reinstatement of mortgages securing Daido and Shinyetsu dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The fiscal agent describes outstanding bonds, government guarantees, and the wartime cancellation of their mortgages. It asks the United States to have Japan restore the original security.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Norman E. Webster
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Addresses Webster’s City of Tokyo sterling bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department explains that American holders should expect treatment comparable to British holders, suggests contacting the Corporation of Foreign Bondholders, and requests ownership and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser routing slip
subfiles.about: Routes correspondence for recording and prompt return.
subfiles.summary: An urgent slip directs that the item be recorded and returned.

subfiles.title: Webster’s notice of debt claim
subfiles.about: Notifies the Department of a debt claim filed with the Office of Alien Property.
subfiles.summary: Webster encloses a copy of his letter to the Assistant Attorney General.

subfiles.title: Webster’s letter to the Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: Submits a debt claim for City of Tokyo 1912 sterling bonds and matured coupons.
subfiles.summary: Webster reports filing Form APC-1C and specifies principal, coupons, and interest claimed.

subfiles.title: Miyo Miyoshi’s citizenship information
subfiles.about: Supplies citizenship information for her bondholder record.
subfiles.summary: Miyoshi says she is an American citizen by birth and provides birth record details.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment to Miyo Miyoshi
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges information about Miyoshi’s Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department will place her information with earlier submissions for possible future use.

subfiles.title: Augusta Greidman’s inquiry about German and Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Asks about interest and redemption on German and Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Greidman seeks information on what the respective governments are doing for bondholders.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to F. O. Mann
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the bank’s concerns about Nippon Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department promises consideration and forwards Mann’s letter to authorities in Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmittal to the Reparations and Restitution Delegation
subfiles.to: Chief, United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Mann’s letter concerning Nippon Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: The letter is sent for possible use in protecting American bondholders’ interests.

subfiles.title: Harris Trust report on Nippon Electric Power bonds
subfiles.from: F. O. Mann, Harris Trust and Savings Bank
subfiles.about: Reports wartime changes that impaired security for Nippon Electric Power dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The bank recounts transfers of mortgaged utility assets, missed payments, conversion of some bonds into yen bonds, government assumption of others, and cancellation of the mortgage. It rejects those unilateral measures and asks that bondholders’ indenture rights be protected in a peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Official envelope
subfiles.about: Official Department of State mailing envelope.
subfiles.summary: Envelope bears official business and postage markings.

subfiles.title: Japan Electric Generation and Transmission report to Harris Trust
subfiles.from: S. Anis, Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company
subfiles.about: Reports wartime treatment of Nippon Electric Power bonds and their security.
subfiles.summary: The company explains unpaid sinking funds, interest deposits in blocked accounts, utility asset transfers, and the 1943 foreign bonds law. It details cancellation, yen conversion, government assumption, and removal of mortgages, with an attached interest funds schedule.

subfiles.title: Teikoku Bank report as successor trustee
subfiles.about: Explains succession to the bond trusteeship and wartime disposition of Nippon Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: The bank describes the transfer of mortgaged properties, assumption of bond obligations by Japan Electric Generation and Transmission, and the later cancellation, yen conversion, and government assumption of bonds under the 1943 law.

subfiles.title: Japan Electric Generation and Transmission follow-up report
subfiles.from: Eiichi Ohnishi, Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company
subfiles.about: Supplies further details on the bonds, transferred assets, and the company’s operations.
subfiles.summary: The company revisits the assumption and conversion of Nippon Electric Power bonds and the effect of the 1943 law on their mortgage. It reports on the mortgaged factory estate, limited war damage, reparations selections, power operations, and finances. It says settlement of bondholders’ claims likely depends on the peace conference.

subfiles.title: Teikoku Bank transmittal of company letters
subfiles.about: Forwards letters from Japan Electric Generation and Transmission and Nichiden Industrial Company.
subfiles.summary: The successor trustee sends two company letters and their enclosures.

subfiles.title: Finance Minister’s order appointing a successor trustee
subfiles.about: Designates Teikoku Bank successor to Mitsui Bank as trustee.
subfiles.summary: The order appoints Teikoku Bank trustee for the electric utility mortgage bonds.

subfiles.title: Law Relating to the Treatment of Foreign Bonds
subfiles.about: Sets rules for converting foreign currency bonds and assuming remaining obligations.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 60 provides for conversion of designated dollar and sterling bonds into yen bonds, cancellation of reacquired bonds, and government assumption of other municipal and corporate bond obligations. It voids mortgages and other original contractual effects after assumption, establishes compensation and guarantee mechanisms, and includes special provisions for Nagoya sterling bonds.

subfiles.title: National City Bank request concerning Ujigawa bonds
subfiles.from: Stewart C. Pratt, National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Requests restoration of security for Ujigawa Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: The fiscal agent describes the mortgaged factory estate and asks SCAP to demand reinstatement of its mortgage. It also flags the Kizugawa Steam Power Plant’s selection for reparations.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Denver National Bank
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds about Oriental Development and Tokyo Electric Light bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department records the bank’s holdings, describes its limited role in defaults, and refers the bank to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Denver National Bank’s bondholding notice
subfiles.about: Reports ownership of Oriental Development and Tokyo Electric bonds.
subfiles.summary: The bank offers further details to help safeguard its two holdings.

subfiles.title: City Bank & Trust Company’s Japanese bond inquiry
subfiles.from: City Bank & Trust Company, Vice President
subfiles.about: Seeks information on Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: The writer reports a $2,000 holding and a claim through the Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: City Bank & Trust Company letter on claim form
subfiles.from: City Bank & Trust Company, Vice President
subfiles.about: Returns an executed debt claim form.
subfiles.summary: The writer thanks the office for Form APC-1C and sends it back completed.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Jessie Goets
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds concerning an Oriental Development Company bond.
subfiles.summary: The Department outlines its limited role, recommends the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, requests purchase and citizenship information, and points Goets toward possible Office of Alien Property debt claims.

subfiles.title: Jessie Goets’s Oriental Development bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Requests information about an Oriental Development Company gold bond.
subfiles.summary: Goets identifies a $500 bond and asks for information about its status.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to E. J. Working
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds concerning Working’s Ujigawa Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes assistance available to holders, refers Working to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and requests additional bond purchase and citizenship details for its records.

subfiles.title: E. J. Working’s Ujigawa bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks what to do about an overdue Ujigawa Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Working notes stopped interest payments and asks whether Japan acquired the company’s property or guaranteed its bonds.

subfiles.title: Charles Harvey Fahs’s Japanese bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks whether two Imperial Japanese Government bonds have value.
subfiles.summary: Fahs reports holding two bonds and coupons unpaid since Pearl Harbor.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Charles Harvey Fahs
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains why the Department cannot value or suggest a sale for Fahs’s bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites the absence of broker transactions in Japanese bonds, refers Fahs to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, requests purchase and citizenship information, and mentions possible debt claims with the Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Belgian bank inquiry about destroyed Japanese bonds
subfiles.from: Banque Belge pour l’Etranger, New York Agency
subfiles.to: Department of State, O. J. McDiarmid
subfiles.about: Asks how to replace Japanese bonds destroyed during the invasion of Belgium.
subfiles.summary: The bank seeks replacement procedures for bonds deliberately burned in May 1940.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Banque Belge pour l’Etranger
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Banque Belge pour l’Etranger, New York Agency
subfiles.about: Suggests a route for seeking replacement of destroyed Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department suggests contacting Belgium’s representative in Tokyo, directly or through the Belgian Embassy.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Keith M. MacEvan
subfiles.about: Begins a response about two Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: The surviving page explains the Department’s limited role and refers MacEvan to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.
